Description: Anchor links should scroll smoothly to target section
Do: Use scroll-behavior: smooth on html element

Description: Fixed nav should not obscure content
Do: Add padding-top to body equal to nav height
Don't: Let nav overlap first section content

Description: Current page/section should be visually indicated
Do: Highlight active nav item with color/underline
Don't: No visual feedback on current location

Description: Users expect back to work predictably
URLs should reflect current state for sharing
Show user location in site hierarchy
Do: Use for sites with 3+ levels of depth

Description: Too many animations cause distraction and motion sickness
Do: Animate 1-2 key elements per view maximum

Description: Animations should feel responsive not sluggish
Don't: Use animations longer than 500ms for UI

Description: Respect user's motion preferences
Show feedback during async operations
Don't: Leave UI frozen with no feedback

Description: Hover effects don't work on touch devices
Don't: Rely only on hover for important actions

Description: Infinite animations are distracting
Some CSS properties trigger expensive repaints
Do: Use transform and opacity for animations

Description: Linear motion feels robotic
Do: Use ease-out for entering ease-in for exiting

Description: Stacking context conflicts cause hidden elements
Hidden overflow can clip important content
Do: Test all content fits within containers

Description: Fixed elements can overlap or be inaccessible
Do: Account for safe areas and other fixed elements
Code Example Good: Fixed nav + fixed bottom with gap

Description: New stacking contexts reset z-index
Do: Understand what creates new stacking context
Don't: Expect z-index to work across contexts

Description: Layout shift when content loads is jarring
100vh can be problematic on mobile browsers
Do: Use dvh or account for mobile browser chrome

Description: Content too wide is hard to read
Don't: Let text span full viewport width

Description: Small buttons are hard to tap accurately
Adjacent touch targets need adequate spacing
Custom gestures can conflict with system
Do: Avoid horizontal swipe on main content

Description: 300ms tap delay feels laggy
Accidental refresh is frustrating
Tactile feedback improves interaction feel
Do: Use for confirmations and important actions

Description: Keyboard users need visible focus indicators
Do: Use visible focus rings on interactive elements

Description: Visual feedback on interactive elements
Do: Change cursor and add subtle visual change
Don't: No hover feedback on clickable elements

Description: Show immediate feedback on press/click
Clearly indicate non-interactive elements
Prevent double submission during async actions
Do: Disable button and show loading state

Description: Users need to know when something fails
Do: Show clear error messages near problem

Description: Confirm successful actions to users
Do: Show success message or visual change

Description: Prevent accidental destructive actions
Text must be readable against background
Don't convey information by color alone
Do: Use icons/text in addition to color

Description: Images need text alternatives
Do: Descriptive alt text for meaningful images

Description: Screen readers use headings for navigation
Don't: Skip heading levels or misuse for styling

Description: Interactive elements need accessible names
All functionality accessible via keyboard
Don't: Keyboard traps or illogical tab order

Description: Content should make sense when read aloud
Do: Use semantic HTML and ARIA properly

Description: Inputs must have associated labels
Do: Use label with for attribute or wrap input

Description: Error messages must be announced
Do: Use aria-live or role=alert for errors

Description: Allow keyboard users to skip navigation
Do: Provide skip to main content link
Don't: No skip link on nav-heavy pages

Description: Large images slow page load
Load content as needed
Do: Lazy load below-fold images and content

Description: Large bundles slow initial load
Repeat visits should be fast
Web fonts can block rendering
External scripts can block rendering
Large JavaScript slows interaction
CSS/JS can block first paint
Every input needs a visible label
Do: Always show label above or beside input

Description: Errors should appear near the problem
Don't: Single error message at top of form

Description: Validate as user types or on blur
Do: Validate on blur for most fields

Description: Use appropriate input types
Do: Use email tel number url etc

Description: Help browsers autofill correctly
Mark required fields clearly
Let users see password while typing
Confirm form submission status
Inputs should look interactive
Don't: Inputs that look like plain text

Description: Show appropriate keyboard for input type
Design for mobile then enhance for larger
Do: Start with mobile styles then add breakpoints

Description: Test at all common screen sizes
Mobile layouts need touch-sized targets
Text must be readable on all devices
Set viewport for mobile devices
Avoid horizontal scrolling
Images should scale with container
Tables can overflow on mobile
Do: Use horizontal scroll or card layout

Description: Adequate line height improves readability
Long lines are hard to read
Consistent type hierarchy aids scanning
Fonts should load without layout shift
Body text needs good contrast
Do: Use darker text on light backgrounds

Description: Headings should stand out from body
Show system status during waits
Guide users when no content exists
Help users recover from errors
Show progress for multi-step processes
Transient messages for non-critical info
Confirm successful actions
Handle long content gracefully
Do: Truncate with ellipsis and expand option

Description: Use locale-appropriate date formats
Format large numbers for readability
Show realistic placeholders during dev
Users should be able to skip tutorials
Help users find results faster
Dead ends frustrate users
Editing one by one is tedious
Users need to know they talk to AI
Waiting for full text is slow
Do: Stream text response token by token

Description: Elements should respond to eye tracking before pinch
UI needs Z-depth to separate content from environment
Video consumes massive data and energy
Heavy 3D/Image assets increase carbon footprint
AI needs user feedback to improve
Parallax/Scroll-jacking causes nausea

Description: When AI outputs have variable certainty, communicate confidence levels visually. Never show uncertain AI output with the same visual weight as verified data. Use confidence bars, hedging language, or color coding.
Do: Show a confidence indicator (low/med/high) beside AI-generated fields; use amber for uncertain, neutral for confident
Don't: Don't present AI-generated data identically to human-verified data — users will trust it incorrectly

Description: AI-generated content that will be committed (saved, sent, published) must require explicit human confirmation. Never auto-commit AI output. Always show an editable preview before any AI result becomes permanent.
Do: Show AI draft in an editable field; require explicit Save/Confirm action; allow full edit before committing
Don't: Don't auto-save AI output without user review; don't disable the editing field when showing AI suggestion
Code Example Good: <AIPreview editable value={aiDraft} onConfirm={save} onEdit={setDraft} label="Review before saving" />
Code Example Bad: // Bad: await api.save(aiResponse) // saved without user review

Description: CMD+K command palette is a power feature. Surface its existence with a subtle hint (search bar placeholder, keyboard shortcut badge in header) without forcing it on new users. Do not require it for primary tasks.
Do: Add CMD+K hint in header search bar placeholder; show keyboard badge in navigation; use it as a shortcut not a requirement
Don't: Don't hide all navigation behind CMD+K only; don't show a tutorial popup on first visit
Code Example Bad: <button onClick={openAll}>Use CMD+K to navigate</button> // Only option

Description: Design collaborative UIs to prevent conflicts, not just resolve them. Show who is editing what in real time. Lock or warn before two users edit the same field. Optimistic UI must reconcile divergence gracefully.
Do: Show field-level editing locks (dim + avatar badge); warn before overwriting; resolve conflicts with last-write-wins + history
Don't: Don't silently overwrite another user's edit; don't show merge conflicts as raw JSON diffs
Code Example Bad: // Bad: await api.save(localValue) // last-write-wins silently overwrites

Description: Progressive disclosure reduces overwhelm but must never hide information users need to make a decision. Primary action, price, key risks, and required fields must always be visible. Only secondary/advanced options are hidden.
Do: Show price, main CTA, and required fields always visible; hide advanced options behind Show more
Don't: Don't hide mandatory fields, pricing, or cancellation terms behind a Show more
Code Example Bad: <Collapsible trigger='See all fields'><Price /><RequiredField /></Collapsible> // Bad — required info hidden

Description: Empty states are conversion moments. Every empty state must have: a clear reason why it is empty, an illustration or icon (optional), and a primary action button that directly creates the first item. Never show a plain 'No data' message.
Do: Show illustration + headline + 1-sentence explanation + primary CTA button ('Create your first X')
Don't: Don't show only 'No records found' with no action; don't use generic 'empty' wording
Code Example Good: <EmptyState icon={<FileIcon />} title="No invoices yet" description="Create your first invoice to get started." action={<Button>Create Invoice</Button>} />
Code Example Bad:
No data found.

// No action, no context

Description: Validate on blur (when user leaves a field), not on keypress. Show success state on valid blur. Show error only after the user has had a chance to complete the field. Never show errors on a pristine/untouched field.
Do: Validate onBlur; show green check on valid; show red error message below field on invalid blur; re-validate onChange after first error
Don't: Don't validate onKeyDown before user finishes typing; don't show errors on untouched fields on submit
Code Example Good: input.addEventListener('blur', () => { if (!isValid(input.value)) showError(); else showSuccess(); }); // Re-validate on change after first error
Code Example Bad: input.addEventListener('keydown', validateField); // Bad — errors flash while typing

Description: Every drag-and-drop interaction must have a keyboard-accessible alternative. Drag to reorder must also work with arrow keys + Enter. Drag to delete must have a Delete key or button alternative. WCAG 2.5.1 requires this.
Do: Implement keyboard reorder (arrow keys change position, Enter/Space picks up/drops); show keyboard hint on focus
Don't: Don't ship drag-only interactions without keyboard equivalent; don't hide the keyboard instructions
Code Example Good: // dnd-kit: useSortable provides keyboard sensors out of the box. keyboardSensor = useSensor(KeyboardSensor, { coordinateGetter: sortableKeyboardCoordinates })
Code Example Bad: // Bad: draggable={true} with no keyboard alternative

Description: For SaaS onboarding, a persistent progress checklist (X of 5 steps complete) outperforms sequential tooltip tours. Tooltip tours break when users skip steps or navigate away. Checklists are revisitable and skippable.
Do: Show an onboarding checklist in sidebar/dashboard with clickable items; mark completed; show % progress; allow dismiss
Don't: Don't use a linear tooltip tour that blocks the UI; don't require completing step N before step N+1 if steps are independent
Code Example Bad: <Tooltip force-open target='#nav-item'>First, click here</Tooltip> // Breaks on navigation

Description: Charts and data widgets must have three states styled to the same quality: loading (skeleton matching chart shape), empty (actionable empty state), and error (retry action). A spinner in a chart slot is worse than a content-shaped skeleton.
Do: Build BarChartSkeleton, LineChartSkeleton etc. that match chart proportions; show chart-shaped skeleton during load
Don't: Don't show a generic spinner in a 400px tall chart slot; don't show blank white space

Description: For mobile apps with 3-5 primary sections, always use a bottom navigation bar. Hamburger menus hide navigation and reduce discoverability by 50%+. Reserve hamburger only for secondary/overflow items (6+ items).
Do: Use bottom nav tabs for 3-5 primary sections; icons + labels; active state clear; safe-area-inset-bottom respected
Don't: Don't use hamburger menu for primary navigation on mobile; don't put more than 5 items in bottom nav
Code Example Bad: <HamburgerMenu primaryLinks={[home, search, profile]} /> // Primary nav hidden

Description: Apply optimistic updates for all user-initiated state changes with near-certain success (like/unlike, reorder, delete, toggle). Update the UI immediately, then confirm or revert on API response. Waiting 300-800ms before UI responds feels broken.
Do: Update local state immediately on user action; send API request in background; revert with toast if API fails
Don't: Don't wait for API response before updating UI on simple toggles; don't show a loading spinner for sub-500ms operations
Code Example Good: // React Query: useMutation({ onMutate: async (newVal) => { await queryClient.cancelQueries(['item']); const prev = queryClient.getQueryData(['item']); queryClient.setQueryData(['item'], newVal); return { prev }; }, onError: (err, _, ctx) => queryClient.setQueryData(['item'], ctx.prev) })
Code Example Bad: // Bad: await api.toggle(id); then setLocalState() // 800ms lag visible to user

Description: When a modal opens, focus must move to the first interactive element inside it. When a modal closes, focus must return to the trigger button. When a page section updates (SPA route change), focus must move to the new page heading.
Do: Use dialog role with autoFocus on first input; return focus to trigger on close; announce route changes to screen readers
Don't: Don't leave focus on the element behind a modal overlay; don't forget to return focus on close
Code Example Good: // Radix Dialog does this automatically. Manual: useEffect(() => { dialogRef.current?.querySelector('input,button')?.focus(); }, [open]);
Code Example Bad: // Bad: <div role='dialog'> with no focus management — keyboard users are stranded

Issue: Never Convey State by Color Alone
Description: Color alone must never be the only indicator of state. Error fields need both red color AND an error icon AND a text message. Success needs both green AND a check icon. Required fields need both red asterisk AND label text. WCAG 1.4.1.
Do: Combine color + icon + text label for every state: error (red + X icon + message), success (green + check + message)
Don't: Don't use color-only indicators; red border alone is insufficient for colorblind users

Description: Every screen should have exactly one primary CTA. When there are multiple equal CTAs, users freeze (paradox of choice). Demote secondary actions visually (ghost button, text link, dropdown). The primary button must be the highest contrast element on screen.
Do: One solid primary button per screen; secondary actions as outline/ghost; tertiary as text links or in overflow menu
Don't: Don't show two solid primary buttons side-by-side; don't give equal visual weight to primary and secondary CTAs

Description: Employee profile cards must show: avatar (with fallback initials), name, designation, department, and quick-action buttons. Never show sensitive data (salary, PAN, bank) on cards visible in lists. Quick actions: message, view profile, edit (if permitted).
Do: Show avatar (64px), name bold, designation muted, department badge, 2-3 quick action icons; use initials fallback for missing avatar
Don't: Don't show salary, bank details, or PAN on list cards; don't use generic placeholder avatars
Code Example Good: <EmployeeCard avatar={emp.photo || initials(emp.name)} name={emp.name} designation={emp.designation} department={emp.department} actions={[viewProfile, message]} />

Description: Leave balance widgets must show: leave type, available days, used days, and total quota. Use color coding (green for available, amber for low, red for exhausted). Show accrual date if applicable. Never show negative balance without explanation.
Do: Circular or bar progress for each leave type; color-code: green >50%, amber 20-50%, red <20%; show "Accrues on [date]" for pending
Don't: Don't show raw numbers without visual progress; don't allow negative display without note
Code Example Good: <LeaveBalance type="Casual" available={5} used={7} total={12} status="low" accrualDate="1st Apr" />
Code Example Bad:
CL: 5

// No context, no visual, no status

Description: Attendance views must use calendar heatmaps with clear color coding: present (green), absent (red), half-day (amber), holiday (blue), weekend (gray). Show legend. Allow click to view day details. Mobile: show week view by default.
Do: Month calendar grid with color-coded cells; legend visible; hover/click for day details; filter by status; mobile week view
Don't: Don't use same color for all days; don't require scrolling to see legend; don't hide weekends

Description: Payslips must clearly separate: earnings (left/top), deductions (right/bottom), and net pay (prominent). Use table layout for line items. Show YTD totals. Provide download PDF button. Never expose payslip in URLs or logs.
Do: Two-column or stacked layout; earnings green-tinted header, deductions red-tinted; net pay large and bold; PDF download; print-friendly
Don't: Don't mix earnings and deductions in one list; don't show payslip ID in URL; don't log salary amounts

Description: Approval workflows must show: current stage (highlighted), completed stages (checkmark), pending stages (dimmed), and timeline. Show approver name and timestamp for completed stages. Pending stage shows expected approver. Allow one-click approve/reject with required comment for reject.
Do: Horizontal or vertical stepper; completed=green check; current=pulsing; pending=gray; show approver+timestamp; approve button primary, reject button destructive with required comment
Don't: Don't hide the workflow stages; don't allow reject without comment; don't show only current stage

Description: Org charts must support: expand/collapse nodes, search by name, zoom controls, and export. Show photo+name+designation per node. Highlight current user. Support both tree and list views. Large orgs: lazy-load branches.
Do: Tree with expand/collapse; search filters and highlights; zoom controls; photo+name+title per node; current user highlighted; list view toggle; lazy-load for 500+ nodes
Don't: Don't load entire org tree upfront for large orgs; don't use only horizontal scroll
Code Example Good: <OrgChart data={orgData} currentUser={userId} onSearch={filter} lazyLoad={nodes > 500} views={[tree, list]} />

Description: Bulk actions (salary processing, mass leave approval, bulk termination) must show: count of affected records, summary of action, affected employee names (up to 10, then +N more), and require explicit confirmation. Show processing progress for long operations.
Do: Modal with affected count prominent; list up to 10 names; "+N more" link to full list; action summary; confirm button requires typing "CONFIRM" for destructive; progress bar for processing
Don't: Don't process bulk actions without confirmation modal; don't hide affected count; don't allow one-click destructive bulk actions
Code Example Good: <BulkConfirmModal action="Process Salary" affected={employees} count={150} destructive={false} onConfirm={process} showProgress={true} />

Description: HRMS dashboard KPIs must show: metric name, current value (large), trend arrow (up/down), comparison period, and sparkline. Group related KPIs. Click to drill down. Role-based visibility (HR sees all, Manager sees team only, Employee sees personal).
Do: Card with metric name top; large value center; trend arrow with % change; sparkline bottom; click for details; 4-6 KPIs per row; role-filtered data
Don't: Don't show all metrics to all roles; don't display without trend context; don't exceed 12 KPIs on one dashboard
Code Example Good: <KPITile metric="Attrition Rate" value={4.2} trend="down" change={-0.5} period="vs last month" sparkline={data} onClick={drillDown} />
Code Example Bad:
Attrition: 4.2%

// No trend, no context, no interactivity
